meta.heading: Round 8: the canvas, and sign-offs for tickets
meta.intro: Two working mockups from your notes: the Canvas with stacks and a filing cabinet, and closing messages that some tickets need. Everything is made-up sample data. Round 7's decisions are already built into 0.2.0.

r8-canvas.title: The Canvas with stacks and drawers
body: The free canvas you picked in round 4, with two ways to keep it from turning into a mess. **Stacks:** drop a card on another card and they become a pile with a count. Click a pile to fan it out; drag a card out to take it off. Double-click a pile's name to rename it. **Drawers:** the cabinet on the left. Drop a card or a whole pile on a drawer and it slides in, off the desk. Open the drawer to see what's inside or put something back.
Filing only tidies the desk. Filed things still show up in Find, and their hours still count on the timesheet.
Want to click around? [Open the interactive canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/RgWr24Jb5WYJrb5BLBk56p).

figures.caption: Two piles: **Network refresh** (dropped one card on another) and **SSL renewals**, fanned out by clicking it.
The **Reference** drawer opened, after dropping the scrap onto it.
After **Tidy into stacks** and **Arrange as timeline**: piles sit at their newest date.

bullets: **Tidy into stacks** piles loose cards by project in one click. Cards with no project stay loose.
**Arrange as timeline** still works: piles sit at their newest date, and **Back to my layout** puts everything back.
Each project gets a drawer automatically. You can add plain drawers, like **Reference**, for things that aren't a project.

options.value: Every project, plus folders I make

questions.placeholder: e.g. colour the piles, zoom, a pile per week

r8-canvas.pick: Stacks and drawers, with a drawer for every project plus your own folders, and the Tidy button. Piles keep today's work at hand; drawers keep the desk clear without hiding anything from Find.

r8-signoff.title: Sign-offs, take 2: a list of your own responses on every ticket
body: You're right: Shiftbook only knows the ticket number and what you logged against it, so it can't guess what a ticket needs. Instead, every ticket in the tray gets a small **✎**. Press it and your own list of saved responses opens. Pick one, fill the gaps, press **Copy**. Shiftbook fills in only what it really knows: the ticket number, the date, the title you logged and the hours.

Responses you've used with the same kind of ticket before (every **CHG**, say) float to the top, so the right one is usually first. **+ New response** saves a new one for next time. If you want, Settings can still mark certain kinds of ticket in yellow as a reminder; that part is optional.
Want to try it? [Open the interactive sign-offs](https://claude.ai/artifact/WrjjyPhuVGAHDoYgRYSPkj).

figures.caption: **✎** pressed on **CHG0012345**: the responses used with CHG before are on top; the chosen one is filled in except the part only you know.

options.why: Say what's off in the note.

questions.legend: Yellow reminder for certain kinds of ticket
A few kinds of response you'd add first? Describe them; don't paste real ones.
questions.placeholder: e.g. fixed and confirmed, no reply from user, change done

r8-signoff.pick: Yes, with the yellow reminder as an option. It needs no access to your ticket system, so nothing leaves your computer.
r8-signoff.reply: Agreed. Take 2 drops the guessing: you pick from your own list of responses, and Shiftbook only fills in what it actually knows.

r8-boards.title: Boards inside boards, a List view of the same thing, and an Archive
body: Your idea: any card can be a **board** you step into, with its own canvas. The background takes on that board's colour, so you always know you're inside something, and the breadcrumbs at the top show where (Desk › Meetings › Weekly ops). Double-click a folder card to go in; click a breadcrumb to come back out.

Boards aren't only projects. Shiftbook starts you with **Meetings** (a board per meeting series, holding each week's notes), **Daily notes** and **Projects**, and you can make a board out of anything, like **Reference**. Jots and loose notes can sit right on the Desk.
**Without the canvas:** the List view shows the same board as a list, sub-boards first, then notes newest first. The left side is the same tree in both views, so switching never loses your place.

**Archive** sits at the bottom of the tree. Archive anything by hand, or let old daily notes go there by themselves. Archived things still turn up in Find, and **Bring back** puts them where they were.
Want to click around? [Open the interactive boards](https://claude.ai/artifact/9dYUao8KyH3mvUD9YqbBd8).

figures.caption: The Desk: boards look like folders with a peek of what's inside; loose jots and daily notes sit beside them.
Inside **Desk › Meetings › Weekly ops**: the amber tint tells you which board you're in.
The same board in **List** view: newest meeting first.
The **Archive**: one daily note archived automatically, one by hand, both with Bring back.

bullets: Stacks and drawers from the card above still work inside any board. A drawer is simply a board kept in the tree instead of on the desk.

options.why: Say what's off in the note.

options.value: Meetings, with a board per series

questions.legend: Daily notes go to the Archive by themselves after

r8-boards.pick: Yes, with Meetings, Daily notes and Projects made for you, and daily notes archived after 2 weeks. You can change all of it in Settings.
